note: Phrases in one minor pentatonic position over drums and bass, ended first on the root and then on the minor 3rd, so the learner hears how the last note decides whether a phrase sounds finished. The position is described the first time and named by no number; the key and tempo move (any key, 70 to 90 bpm), and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same.

exercise.title: End on a different note
exercise.why: The bass of the backing track keeps coming back to the root, so a phrase that ends on the root settles with it, and a phrase that ends on the minor 3rd leaves the ear waiting.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track: drums and bass in {{=key}}. Under it is the neck with the notes of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale: each dot is a note to play, and {{1}} and {{b3}} are ringed.
Make up short phrases that end on {{1}}, then phrases that end on {{b3}}. Listen for which ending stops the phrase and which one leaves it hanging.
Then choose the ending for each phrase before you start it.
{{?key}}In another key the position sits on other frets, and {{1}} and {{b3}} keep their places inside it.
